objective: Reconcile the Zuri documentation structure and align docs:graph/docs:preflight with the canonical per-ID record registry, filesystem indexes, and source-linked domain SRS profile; correct lifecycle and link findings, remove false fixture edges, and reduce repeat filesystem root checks without weakening scan coverage or rewriting unresolved requirements.
acceptance: AGENTS.md points writers to one current documentation structure standard and requires filesystem enumeration before creating or replacing documents.
The standard defines the product, canonical requirements, domain, service, decision, plan, roadmap, operations, and historical artifact boundaries without creating a second requirements source.
A domain SRS profile uses linked canonical requirements and preserves local clauses until individually reconciled; service documents explain execution and verification boundaries.
Plan and roadmap indexes identify the sole live delivery-state source and classify the 24-week Markdown and HTML artifacts without claiming stale data is current.
All 41 tracked direct files under docs/ at the reviewed base appear in a root-file register with declared status or an explicit unresolved classification.
All 20 tracked direct folders under docs/ at the reviewed base appear in a directory register with their existing entrypoint or an explicit missing-index note.
Current missing domain SRS coverage is recorded as a gap without inventing ownership, requirements, or acceptance.
Canonical IDs, local user changes, and historical approval evidence are preserved; replaced partial workflow text remains recoverable in Git history.

The direct-root register gives every one of the 41 files a role, reader evidence, and an explicit keep/history/conflict disposition; source conflicts and partial duplicates are reconciled only where accepted decisions or exact implementation evidence support it.
Every direct docs/ folder resolves to a local README, generated navigation, canonical ID index, or archive entrypoint; no duplicate folder catalog is added where a canonical index already exists.
The S-01 runbook path no longer carries a conflicting partial workflow copy and clearly points to the candidate source and active delivery policy.
The Workspace design note distinguishes implemented model/authority evidence from the remaining FR-066 UX correction, and its source paths resolve to the current monorepo locations.
GoVibe integration and gap-analysis documents are labeled as historical proposal/snapshot material; their relationship to ADR-009 and ADR-024 is stated without conflating those decisions.

Graph requirement and feature nodes, lifecycle, and membership are derived from canonical per-ID records located by registry/document-registry/index.json; PRD-SDD-v1.0.md and FEATURES.md are not semantic input sources.
Preflight validates canonical record and FEAT-to-FR consistency from the same records, without inferring domain ownership from a folder, service, or feature name.

Preflight checks the direct docs root-file and directory registers against live filesystem entries, excluding only named generated projections, and reports unregistered entries without deleting or moving files.

An SRS that declares doc_type: domain-srs-view is checked against the source-linked profile and canonical links; legacy SRS files without this marker remain untouched, no SRS is mandated for every domain, and no owner is inferred.
New focused tests prove canonical record authority, registry/index mismatch handling, inventory-register drift detection, and SRS profile validation; tests pass after an observed failing run.

Canonical graph lifecycle uses the same strict retirement semantics as the ID ledger; retired feature records retain their ADR successor edge and current/deferred requirement prose is not misread as retirement.
Workspace-root lookup is stable and cached per process, preserving app-local and repository-shared path mappings while avoiding repeated filesystem probes.
Synthetic requirement IDs in fixtures and stale @tested paths do not create dangling graph edges; graph reports zero dangling edges without reducing source or test enumeration.

Generated uncommitted corpus/report outputs are described as build commands instead of broken navigation links; missing approval/evidence artifacts remain explicitly reported rather than reconstructed.
mandateReference: Direct user requests to fix the documentation structure and the 2026-10-22 reply explicitly authorizing updates to docs:graph and docs:preflight to align with the new system.
